I.522 Auditing and Assurance 
• In addition to the audit of financial st atements, the auditor has other reporting 
responsibilities required under the Compan ies Act, 1956 and/or other regulatory 
requirements.  
INDEPENDENT AUDITOR’S REPORT  
To the Members of ABC Company Limited  
Report on the Financial Statements  
We have audited the accompanying financial statements of ABC Company Limited (“the Company”), 
which comprise the Balance Sheet as at March 31, 20XX, and the Statement of Profit and Loss and 
Cash Flow Statement for the year then ended, and a summary of significant accounting policies and 
other explanatory information.  
Management’s Responsibility fo r the Financial Statements  
Management is responsible for the preparation of these financial statements that give a true and fair 
view of the financial position, financial performance and cash flows of the Company in accordance with 
the Accounting Standards referred to in sub-section (3C) of section 211 of the Companies Act, 1956 
(“the Act”). This responsibility includes the design, implementation and maintenance of internal control 
relevant to the preparation and fair presentation of the financial statements that are free from material 
misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.  
Auditor’s Responsibility  
Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audit. We 
conducted our audit in accordance with the Standards on Auditing issued by the Institute of Chartered 
Accountants of India. Those Standards require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and 
perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance ab out whether the financial statements are free from 
material misstatement.  
An audit involves performing procedures to obtain audit evidence about the amounts and disclosures in 
the financial statements. The procedures selected depend on the auditor’s judgment, including the 
assessment of the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to fraud or 
error. In making those risk assessments, the audi tor considers internal control relevant to the 
Company’s preparation and fair presentation of th e financial statements in order to design audit 
procedures that are appropriate in the circumstan ces. An audit also includes evaluating the 
appropriateness of accounting policies used and the reasonableness of the accounting estimates made 
by management, as well as evaluating the overal l presentation of the financial statements.  
We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropria te to provide a basis for 
our qualified audit opinion.

anomaly_flags.regulatory_response:
1. The specific clause/section that governs this anomaly: [caro_2020.pdf, Page 6, Para 3(ix)] and relevant sections of the Companies Act, 2013, particularly sections related to loans and borrowings.
2. What the regulation requires in this situation: The regulation requires the company to disclose defaults in repayment of loans or other borrowings, including the period and amount of default. Additionally, the auditor must verify if the company has complied with provisions related to loans and borrowings.
3. Recommended audit procedure for the auditor: The auditor must verify the company's borrowings, including off-balance-sheet debt, and check for any defaults in repayment. The auditor should also review the company's compliance with sections 185 and 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, regarding loans, investments, guarantees, and security.
4. Draft audit observation sentence: "The company has reported finance costs of Rs. 1,048.00, but no borrowings were disclosed, indicating a potential off-balance-sheet debt or extraction gap, which requires further clarification and verification. The company should disclose any defaults in repayment of loans or borrowings as per the regulatory requirements."
